product: Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan

themes.label: Identity theft and unauthorized loans or accounts
themes.description: Consumers allege loans or accounts were opened in their names without authorization and that the lender did not cancel, dispute, or remove them.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a $20,000 loan was fraudulently obtained using their personal information and an unverified identification card, with the bank refusing to acknowledge the fraud, denying the dispute claim, and failing to remove the account from credit reporting despite police reports and multiple agency filings.

Consumer claims an unauthorized person opened a lease account using the consumer's social security number and identifying information without permission, and the company has failed to cancel the account after four fraud department requests.
Consumer claims an account was fraudulently opened in their name without authorization and used for transactions totaling $220.

themes.label: Misrepresented terms in solar and point-of-sale financing
themes.description: Consumers allege sellers or lenders misrepresented savings, tax credits, payment amounts, fees, or promised deliverables when originating financed purchases.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a solar loan was issued based on misrepresentations about the system's expected performance and projected savings, which failed to materialize, and the lender has not resolved the formal dispute after requesting investigation and payment forbearance.

Consumer claims a lender engaged in compromised loan verification procedures, misrepresented tax credit and payment terms to induce loan signing, and failed to transparently disclose inflated dealer fees that increased the loan principal.

Consumer alleges they were fraudulently induced into a loan contract through misrepresentations about rebates and cost savings that were not delivered, and seeks full loan rescission and refund of all payments made.

themes.label: Denials with unclear reasons or alleged bias
themes.description: Consumers allege loan applications were denied without specific reasons, on allegedly discriminatory grounds, or due to processing errors the lender would not correct.

examples.summary: Consumer claims that a lender denied a joint personal loan application based on the applicants' unmarried marital status, then issued a falsified credit denial letter citing reasons not previously discussed and allegedly created an unauthorized single-applicant loan file.
Consumer claims a lender denied a personal loan application after requesting personal information and refused to retract the application, alleging discriminatory conduct and securities fraud.
Consumer claims loan application was denied with an Adverse Action Notice lacking specific reasons, and subsequent attempts to contact the lender via provided email and phone were unsuccessful.

themes.label: Identity verification failures and account restrictions
themes.description: Consumers allege they were blocked, frozen, or closed out of accounts or purchases due to identity verification problems or unexplained decisions.

examples.summary: Consumer's account was frozen without adequate explanation and remained frozen for over 10 days despite submitting requested documentation four times; customer service failed to respond to complaints and supervisor requests within promised timeframes and continued requesting documents already provided.

Consumer claims their Cash App account and their son's account were closed for alleged rule violations that the consumer denies committing, and the company refused to explain the specific violation despite multiple appeals.

Consumer claims that despite being an active customer with paid-on-time loans, the lender declined purchase attempts citing inability to verify identity, yet continued accepting payments, and delayed escalation resolution.

themes.label: Disbursement, rescission and approval process disputes
themes.description: Consumers allege lenders mishandled approval timelines, changed offers, disbursed funds improperly, or failed to honor cancellation or rescission requests.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a financing institution disbursed full loan proceeds without verifying project completion or regulatory approval, and placed a UCC-1 lien on the property despite the underlying solar installation being incomplete and non-functional, preventing the consumer from refinancing or selling their home.

Consumer claims that after completing an online loan application and being presented with both a $15,000 unsecured and $30,000 secured loan option following a credit inquiry, a representative subsequently stated only the $30,000 secured loan was available.

Consumer claims a bank provided a 2-3 week closing timeline for an SBA 7a business loan, but months later has refused to provide a closing date despite consumer submitting all requested documentation, resulting in indefinite delays and unclear next steps.

brief.headline: Loan origination complaints edge up, with solar financing and denial-reason signals standing out
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints in the 'Getting the loan' cluster for payday, title, personal, or advance loans are modestly accelerating. The recent monthly average is 173 against a baseline of 152 (velocity 1.1338, rank 13 of 79), and August 2026 reached 202 complaints, the highest in the 12-month series. In a sample of 38 narratives analyzed by an earlier AI step, consumers allege misrepresented terms in solar and point-of-sale financing, denials with unclear or allegedly biased reasons, identity theft and unauthorized loans, identity verification lockouts, and disbursement or rescission disputes. These are unverified claims.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers applying for personal, point-of-sale, solar, and other installment or advance loans. About 18.4% of the AI-reviewed sample were flagged as potentially vulnerable consumers. Complaints are geographically concentrated in CA (15.2%), TX (10.8%), and FL (10.6%). Companies with notable over-representation relative to size include SoFi Technologies (lift 3.032), Truist Financial (2.789), Paramount GR Holdings (2.444), Fifth Third Financial (2.425), and Solar Servicing Holdings (1.509). Affirm (1.006), OneMain (0.844), and Klarna (0.833) are not over-represented despite high or notable counts.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: weak controls at the point of origination, particularly in third-party or dealer-sourced financing, may be producing disputes about how terms, savings, and fees were described. Separately, adverse action communications may not give applicants specific, understandable reasons, and identity verification and fraud-dispute workflows may be too slow or inconsistent when accounts are frozen or alleged fraudulent loans must be cancelled.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Review point-of-sale and dealer or merchant oversight, including origination call verification and disclosure of fees and payment terms. Also review adverse action notice content and delivery, the fair lending monitoring of denials, identity verification and account-freeze escalation timelines, fraud and identity-theft dispute handling, and rescission or cancellation request processing.
brief.regulatory_area: Consumer lending origination practices, including disclosure and marketing of loan terms, adverse action notices, fair lending in credit decisions, and identity theft and fraud dispute handling
evidence: Recent monthly average of 173 complaints versus a baseline monthly average of 152 (velocity 1.1338, rank 13 of 79).
August 2026 recorded 202 complaints, up from 149 in June and 168 in July.
Monthly counts were 96 in both October and November 2025 versus 150 or more in four of the six baseline months (Dec 2025 to May 2026).
SoFi Technologies has a lift of 3.032 on 25 complaints; Truist Financial has a lift of 2.789 on 23 complaints.
Paramount GR Holdings has the highest count at 67 complaints, with a lift of 2.444; Fifth Third Financial has a lift of 2.425 on 13 complaints.
Affirm has 61 complaints but a lift of only 1.006; Klarna (0.833) and OneMain (0.844) are below 1.
In the 38-narrative AI sample, 29.7% of narratives involved misrepresented terms in solar and point-of-sale financing and 24.3% involved denials with unclear reasons or alleged bias.
Identity theft and unauthorized loans account for 13.5% of the AI sample; identity verification failures and account restrictions and disbursement or rescission disputes account for 16.2% each.
Mean AI-assessed severity is 3.76 on a 1 to 5 scale, with 18.4% of the sample flagged as vulnerable consumers.
Templated share of recent narratives is 0.0% across 89 narratives in recent months.
CA, TX, and FL account for 15.2%, 10.8%, and 10.6% of complaints respectively.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief does not pin the signal on one company, and the lifts it cites (SoFi 3.032, Truist 2.789, Paramount 2.444) match the data, while Affirm at 1.006 and Klarna at 0.833 are correctly described as not over-represented.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: Templated share is 0.0% across 89 recent narratives, well below the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top state, CA, holds only 15.2% of complaints, and the top company, Paramount, has 67 complaints spread among many firms with at least 10 complaints each, so neither one state nor one company explains the signal.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The AI sample has 38 complaints and there are 89 recent narratives, and the five themes (29.7%, 24.3%, 16.2%, 16.2%, 13.5%) cover the whole sample and support the origination, adverse-action and identity-verification causes named in the brief.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Recent months climb from 149 in June to 168 in July to 202 in August, so the 173 average does not rest on one isolated spike and the series is rising rather than falling.

skeptic.note: All five checks pass: the rise is modest but real, spread across companies and states, not templated, supported by a relevant sample, and still climbing in the latest month.
